newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Chubais says equity market problems solved.
newsitem.headline: Russia Chubais says equity market problems solved.

text.p: Russia has formed a single policy for regulating all its securities markets, First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said on Friday.
"The Russian government has a single policy in regulating the securities market, which is extremely important," Chubais told a news conference.
He said the government had abandoned the principle of regulating the government securities and equities markets separately, removing major elements of uncertainty.
"The Central Bank and the securities commission will both regulate the market, we will not divide the spheres of regulation," Chubais said. "There will be one market, one depository, one registrar."
But Russia has divided regulatory responsibility based on type of market operator.

A document signed by representatives of the Federal Commission for the Securities Market, the Ministry of Finance and the Central Bank allows the the bank to license commercial banks and credit organisations as of January 1, 1998.
Most other operators will be licensed to work on the securities markets by the commission.
Current securities market licences for banks running until October will be extended to January.
